title: Unità 2 · La vita da studente
question: What is my school day like?
words: (ho lezione di, Che ora è?, lo zaino)
workingOn: school subjects, days of the week, and telling time
canDo: I can enter a discussion related to school subjects.
I can talk about my school schedule and activities.
I can write my school schedule.
culture: In Italy, many high schools end around 1 or 2 pm, and some still have class on Saturday morning. Teachers often give oral tests called interrogazioni, where you answer questions in front of the class. Grades go up to 10, and 6 is a passing grade.

grammar.head: avere for school: ho lezione di… · essere for time: È l'una. Sono le due.
tricks: Ho lezione di + subject = I have … class: ho lezione di storia.
One o'clock is singular (È l'una); every other hour is plural (Sono le due, Sono le tre).
Days are lowercase. Il lunedì = on Mondays; domenica is feminine: la domenica.
Studio l'italiano (I study Italian) is a memorized phrase for now; verb charts for -are come later.

sentences: Il lunedì ho lezione di storia.
On Mondays I have history class.
Ho un quaderno e una penna.
I have a notebook and a pen.
On Sundays I don't have school.

forms.why: io → ho. The h is silent.
trick: Ho lezione di storia = I have history class.
Hai una penna? = Do you have a pen?
Ha (with h) = has. A (no h) = to / at.
Every noi form ends in -iamo: abbiamo.
If you are in the group, use noi: abbiamo.

forms.why: le scienze is plural = loro → sono.
One o'clock is singular: È l'una.
Two is plural: Sono le due.
trick: Every hour after one uses Sono le.

forms.why: Eight is plural: Sono le otto.
trick: Sono le otto = It's eight o'clock.

fill.why: io → ho: Ho lezione di storia.

fill.text: Il lunedì noi ___ lezione di arte.

fill.hint: What time is it? → one letter.
fill.why: Che ora è? = What time is it?
La domenica = on Sundays. It's the only feminine day.

read.title: La settimana di Luca
passage: Ciao, sono Luca e sono di Roma.
Hi, I'm Luca and I'm from Rome.
Il lunedì ho lezione di storia e di matematica.
On Mondays I have history and math class.
La storia è difficile, ma l'arte è facile!
History is hard, but art is easy!

questions.why: Il lunedì ho lezione di storia.

listen.en: What class do you have on Mondays?

lines: Hi Marco! What time is it?
It's eight. Do you have class?
And you? What class do you have?
Ho lezione di arte. Che bello! 🎨
I have art class. How nice!

checks: Ho detto una cosa del mio compagno.

finish: Now I know how to talk about my classes, my schedule, and the time!

idiom.it: Avere la testa tra le nuvole
idiom.en: to have your head in the clouds
idiom.ex: Marco, hai la testa tra le nuvole!
idiom.exEn: Marco, your head is in the clouds!
idiom.note: Said to someone who is daydreaming and not paying attention. Italian teachers say it a lot in class!

flags: Studio l'italiano (sentence 12, trick 4) uses studio as a memorized chunk; regular -are conjugation is not taught yet.
Telling time assumes students already know numbers 1-12. Please confirm Unit 1 covers them.

Guide can-do 'I can describe my daily routine' was left out of canDo (schema max is 4, and daily routine needs reflexive and regular verbs students don't have yet). Decide if it should replace another can-do.

Conflict to check: the existing Italiano 1 game already has a unit titled 'Unità 2 · -are e voglio, devo, posso' plus a 'Volere, dovere, potere' unit. This new unit is also Unità 2, and the brief says -are charts are not known yet. Decide numbering and order.
Schedules use il lunedì (= on Mondays, every week) rather than lunedì (= this Monday). Confirm you want the article taught here.
Com'è…? (What is … like?) is assumed known from Unit 1 adjectives.
Culture facts are unverified: end time varies by school, Saturday school is only in some schools, and grade scales usually run about 1/2/3 to 10 with 6 = sufficiente.
Chat uses 'Che bello!' as a chunk (glossed). Reading glosses 'ma' (but) in case it is new.
